title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Preferred repair topology for a fixed-pump, single-DCV, hydraulically pressure-sequenced clamp-and-drill cycle. The circuit keeps the open-circuit reservoir, fixed-displacement pump, relief valve, open-center 4/3 cycle DCV, two double-acting cylinders, and dual pilot-operated clamp load lock. Both sequence valves are the selected externally piloted sequence-valve class: ForwardSequenceValve uses its X port to sense clamp cap pressure before enabling drill advance, and ReverseSequenceValve uses its X port to sense drill rod/retract pressure rise before enabling clamp release. Numeric speeds remain sizing-only, so no flow-control valves are added. The open-center DCV neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents both work lines to tank so the pilot-operated clamp lock can reseat.

motion_control_decisions.phase_name: Clamp hold during drilling and drill return
motion_control_decisions.justification: The clamp must retain the workpiece while the drill advances and retracts. This is a static retention requirement for a horizontal resistive load, not an overrunning dynamic load.
Release motion has no specified speed-control behavior and the horizontal load is not gravity-overrunning; no deliberate throttling, load-independent speed, or regenerative behavior is requested.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Pump draws from tank, branches from Pump.P directly to ReliefValve.P and CycleDCV.P, and ReliefValve.T plus CycleDCV.T return directly to Tank.R. Sequence-valve drains also terminate at Tank.R.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp double-acting cylinder with pilot-check load lock and reverse-sequenced release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Forward A line extends the clamp through the pilot check. Clamp release flow is blocked until ReverseSequenceValve opens from the external drill-retract pressure pilot, then feeds the clamp rod-side line and releases the clamp load lock.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp load lock with pilot release from release line
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Pilot-operated check blocks clamp cap exhaust during hold, with open-center neutral venting both work lines and pilot pressure to tank so the lock can reseat. Clamp hold does not rely on DCV spool leakage.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Hydraulic clamp-before-drill pressure sequence and reverse pressure sequence
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve opens by explicit clamp cap pressure pilot for drill feed. Reverse B line retracts the drill directly while ReverseSequenceValve remains closed; after drill retracted-end pressure rises at its X port, the reverse sequence valve enables clamp release.

ForwardSequenceValve.P receives the forward DCV line, ForwardSequenceValve.X senses clamp cap pressure from ClampPilotCheck.A2, and ForwardSequenceValve.A supplies DrillCylinder.Cap only after the threshold is reached. Its drain is connected to Tank.R and reverse-check behavior preserves the drill cap return path.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Reverse pressure sequence: drill retract before clamp release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReverseSequenceValve.P receives the reverse DCV line, ReverseSequenceValve.X senses DrillCylinder.Rod pressure, and ReverseSequenceValve.A supplies ClampPilotCheck.B1 and the clamp rod side only after drill retracted-end pressure opens the valve. Its drain is connected to Tank.R and reverse-check behavior preserves clamp rod return during clamp advance.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReliefValve opens P to T at the pressure limit to protect the fixed-displacement pump circuit and limit system pressure to the sizing target.

design_decisions.decision: Retained a fixed-displacement pump with open-circuit relief protection.
design_decisions.rationale: No energy-efficiency or standby unloading requirement is stated; the fixed pump is simple and compatible with the selected open-center DCV neutral unloading path.

design_decisions.decision: Retained an open-center 4/3 DCV as the single cycle command valve.
design_decisions.rationale: Open-center neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents A and B to tank, allowing pilot-pressure decay for the clamp pilot-check load lock. A single forward/reverse DCV lets hydraulic sequence valves enforce order without adding electrical sequencing between functions.

design_decisions.decision: Replaced the forward sequence valve with the externally piloted sequence-valve class.
design_decisions.rationale: The X port explicitly senses clamp cap pressure, proving the clamp-pressure trigger rather than relying on implicit upstream pressure sensing.

design_decisions.decision: Replaced the reverse sequence valve with the externally piloted sequence-valve class.
design_decisions.rationale: The X port explicitly senses drill rod/retract pressure rise at the retracted end condition before enabling clamp release, representing the pressure-based reverse-order trigger with a hydraulic pilot line.

design_decisions.decision: Did not add a position-operated valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected repair follows the pressure-sequenced reverse-order directive: the required trigger is pressure rise after drill retraction, not a position-operated changeover. The available position valve class is not needed for this pressure-triggered release gate.

design_decisions.decision: Used the catalog dual pilot-operated check at the clamp actuator ports for clamp holding.
design_decisions.rationale: The clamp hold must not rely on DCV leakage. The dual pilot-operated check provides low-leakage holding and is released by opposite-line pressure during commanded clamp release.

design_decisions.decision: Did not add flow-control valves for the stated speeds.
design_decisions.rationale: All motion-control decisions classify speed realization as sizing_only; numeric travel, force, and speed targets are deferred to pump and cylinder sizing rather than topology-level throttling.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence covers the generic pump/relief concept, double-acting cylinder directional control for clamp and drill feed, pilot-operated/load-holding principles for the clamp, and a forward pressure-sequence interlock that starts the drill branch only after clamp pressure rises. It is not yet sufficient to design the full topology safely and unambiguously because critical gaps remain: the reservoir-to-pump suction/return reservoir topology is not cited; speed/flow-control placement for the clamp/drill motion profiles is not supported; and the complete multi-actuator cycle/interlock that prevents clamp release until drill retract is not established.

items.rationale: Findings support fixed-displacement pump behavior, relief valve requirement, relief placement near pump outlet, relief discharge to tank, and open-center versus closed-center pump/valve compatibility with citations. However, the need explicitly requires complete suction, return, and reservoir topology; the accumulated finding itself states the reservoir-to-pump suction line was not verified. That missing suction/reservoir connection is critical for a complete open hydraulic circuit.

Supported by cited guidance for a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way/3-position directional valve with P/T/A/B port functions, shifted extend/retract flow paths, and center-position behavior options. The load-holding evidence further warns not to rely on directional spool leakage alone for clamp holding.

Evidence supports clamp advance using a double-acting cylinder/DCV, pressure-sequence transition after clamping pressure rises, and load holding during drilling. It does not yet support any speed/flow-control topology for clamp advance/release, nor does it establish the full automatic transition/interlock for clamp release only after drill retraction.

Cited sources support using a pilot-operated check or other non-leaking load-holding valve in the cylinder/load line, piloted from the opposing work port, and explicitly state that spool valves/closed-port DCVs alone can leak and allow creep. This is enough to choose a leak-resistant clamp holding pattern, though exact final actuator-port mounting detail remains a design refinement.

Supported by cited guidance for a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way/3-position directional valve with pressure, tank, and actuator port connections and opposite shifted positions for extend/retract. Center options and their neutral effects are also documented.

Evidence supports drill-feed extend/retract directional control and a pressure-sequence valve that can prevent drill branch operation until the clamp is pressurized. It does not support drill feed speed regulation, rapid/controlled retract bypass arrangements, or an automatic transition from drilling/feed completion to retract.

The forward interlock clamp-before-drill is well supported by cited pressure-sequence valve sources, including normally closed placement in the second branch and external drain needs. However, the complete sequence/interlock requirement is broader: the accumulated evidence does not show how to enforce drill retract before clamp release or prevent forbidden states such as clamp release while the drill feed is still extended.

Cited evidence supports a leak-resistant holding topology using a pilot-operated check/load-holding valve rather than a directional spool alone, with opposing-line pilot release and consideration of pilot pressure. This directly supports keeping the clamp applied while drilling occurs.

design_issues.description: The reverse-order interlock topology is functionally consistent with the brief and deterministic reverse-sequence directive: CycleDCV.B retracts the drill directly, ReverseSequenceValve remains closed until drill-retract pressure rises, and only then supplies clamp release and the clamp pilot-check release pilot. However, the research package records only general sequence-valve evidence, not an application-specific cited schematic for this exact drill-retract-before-clamp-release pattern. This is not blocking because the pattern is explicitly required by the design directives and is hydraulically plausible.

The clamp cap chamber remains connected to the forward pressure line during the drill-feed phase through the free-flow side of the pilot check, so clamp pressure can rise with later drill-feed/system pressure rather than being independently limited at the clamp threshold. This does not defeat the required clamp-before-drill sequencing or clamp holding, and the brief does not explicitly require a pressure-reducing valve, but if the approximately 4 kN clamp force is intended as an upper bound rather than only a developed-force target, a clamp-branch pressure-reducing/limiting element should be considered.

design_review.summary: No blocking functional topology errors found. The circuit provides open-circuit power and direct relief return, powered extend/retract paths, hydraulic clamp-before-drill pressure sequencing, pilot-check clamp holding with vented neutral, and a separate hydraulic reverse-order interlock for drill retract before clamp release. Remaining issues are nonblocking: evidence for the exact reverse-sequence application is incomplete, and clamp force is not independently pressure-limited if the force target is later treated as a maximum.
